svg.title: The smeared station version says the same thing without committing to a grid interpolation: for every smooth test t in the stated separated window, with ∥t∥∞≤M, the ordered upper error is at most εM Q l∥vl∥. Its finite-cutofflift is bounded, real, signed-equivariant, and sends the unit to the actual reference unit. Its scale and normalization are fixed for all those tests. Enlarging the arity, window and degree and decreasing the error preserves the previous requests. The common-order selection first retains these finite data, then uses (WS4) and finite detecting matrices to obtain all derivative estimates. Thus neither the conditional formulation of a station estimate nor the existence of a two-point comparison is being used as a substitute for the joint estimates (WS13).
